skills.name: create-music-poster
skills.title: Create music poster
skills.summary: Make a music poster / album artwork (single, EP or album cover) for DistroKid and the streaming services from the user's picture(s), in Remotion with the thumbnail eng…
skills.description: Make a music poster / album artwork (single, EP or album cover) for DistroKid and the streaming services from the user's picture(s), in Remotion with the thumbnail engine. It sizes the job to the release (a quick cover for a small single, a fuller exploration for a big one), crops the picture to a correct 1:1 square (outcropping only when the subject doesn't fit, upscaling only when the crop is too small), and explores real alternatives — crops, placements and scale, graphic devices and ideas drawn from the lyrics' meaning and the music's mood — shown first as a small direction board of captioned pictures for the user to pick from, before developing the picked directions into 3000×3000 RGB JPEG covers. Finishing looks (grade, duotone, grain, VHS…) are optional and must never cost the picture its clarity. The art with no text always comes first; well exposed for the song's mood; DistroKid's artwork rules checked. No logo unless asked. Use when the user says "make a music poster", "album art / cover art / single artwork for <song>", "DistroKid cover", "/create-music-poster", or asks for more cover options for a poster job under apps/lyrics_videos/thumbnails/jobs/. Append new user feedback to the log at the bottom.

skills.title: Create thumbnail

skills.description: Make YouTube thumbnails (1280×720) in Remotion from the user's picture or a concept, plus the video's details (title, topic, optionally its transcript), built to be clicked: a giant word, a big lit subject, a simplified background and one accent colour, the channel's logo(s) placed where they strike, fonts chosen with care. It first shows a concept board of 6–8 genuinely different ideas (benchmarked side by side with the user's reference thumbnails at feed size), then makes 3 variants of each concept picked, each labelled with an ID so the user picks one final or three for YouTube's A/B test (Test & Compare). Use when the user says "make a thumbnail", "thumbnail for this video / song / lyric video", "/create-thumbnail", "thumbnail variants", "A/B test thumbnails", or asks for a brand's thumbnail template or more thumbnail options for a job under apps/lyrics_videos/thumbnails/jobs/. For a brand's video it reads the brand's thumbnail.json from pack-brand-kit; also the thumbnail step of a finished lyric video. Append new user feedback to the log at the bottom.

skills.name: make-loudness-remaster
skills.title: Make loudness remaster
skills.summary: Remaster a finished song (a Suno track or any stereo mix) for YouTube and streaming the way the user likes it — keep the song's own mix exactly as it is and only make…
skills.description: Remaster a finished song (a Suno track or any stereo mix) for YouTube and streaming the way the user likes it — keep the song's own mix exactly as it is and only make it louder. It measures the original, builds a loudness ladder in REAPER (a gain-only copy with peaks at -1 dBTP, then -11, -10, -9 and -8 LUFS through one limiter and nothing else), measures what each step costs (deep bass, build-up, punch), lets the user pick by ear, and copies the pick next to the mix as "<title> - final master (-N LUFS).wav". No EQ, compression, clipping, stem remixing or noise cleanup unless the user asks for that one thing. Explains each step in plain words for someone new to mastering. Use when the user says "remaster <song>", "master this track", "make it louder", "louder for YouTube / Spotify / the gym", "loudness options", "/make-loudness-remaster", or gives a song folder (a Suno mix with or without its stems) to master. Append new user feedback to the log at the bottom.

skills.description: Make vertical lyric shorts (9:16 YouTube Shorts / Reels / TikTok) of the user's song in Remotion, in the stacked-type style of the "summer leaves quietly" reel — a short phrase a screen, its words filling the black frame top to bottom in huge ultra-bold lowercase, a word or two a row, every row stretched to the same column width (width-fit), the stack centred and filling the frame top to bottom with only a thin black band above and below (letters never stretched), sometimes one word turned vertical down a side, each word lighting up as it is sung, the footage playing inside the letters (a knockout / text mask) on the punch lines and the other lines set over the footage as lockups (one big highlight word, the small words nested beside its letters), a row in solid colour that opens onto the footage, and dives through a letter into the footage full frame on the music's big moments. It picks the best stretches of the song itself (sung, hook-heavy, clean sentence starts and ends, ideally ending on an instrumental hit), casts the user's footage (or footage from a reference video) line by line, cuts 9:16 clips framed on the subject and renders through the shorts path; reviewed through Revisions (revise-video). Use when the user says "make lyric shorts / reels of my song", "shorts with bold stacked words", "words width-fit with the video inside the letters", "text mask shorts", "shorts like this reference" (stacked-type), "/make-lyrics-shorts-summerstyle-boldwords", or asks to change a short under apps/lyrics_videos/projects/<slug>/shorts/ that imports src/lyricshorts. skills.description: Review and revise a rendered video with the user through mediamake's Video Revision screen (/video-revision) — renders for review at half size (the full-size master once, after sign-off), runs machine checks (preflight) before giving the review link, waits in the background for a revision marked ready, reads the revision files (general comments on the whole video, point comments with stills, range comments across shots, machine notes) under out/<slug>/<slug>.revisions/ (or out/<slug>/live.revisions/ when the user reviewed the project live, before any render: /video-revision?live=<slug>), fixes each comment in the project, replies and resolves, and logs the lessons. Also holds the shared intake rule for look previews (3–4 looks as 8 s clips in one grid, or the whole video; the whole video by default under a minute). Shared by every video-making skill (make-lyrics-video, make-video-music-remix, make-waveform-lyric-video, their variants and shorts, and any make-* video skill to come). Use after a render the user will watch, or when the user says "rev-002 is ready", "check my revision / comments", "act on the revisions", "/revise-video <slug>", or asks to fix notes left in the Revisions screen. Not for image sets (thumbnails, posters: create-thumbnail's /file-revision). Append new user feedback to the log at the bottom.

skills.description: Bring MCPs, skills, apps and the Browse Hack Chrome extension installed from MediaMake up to date, showing the installed and live version numbers and the release notes in between, without asking for an install code again. Use when the user says "update browse hack", "update <an MCP or skill from MediaMake>", "update everything from MediaMake", "check for updates", "what version of <item> do I have", "is <item> up to date", or pastes an "Update <item> from MediaMake" prompt.

skills.name: write-youtube-metadata
skills.title: Write youtube metadata
skills.summary: Write the YouTube title and description for a song on one of the user's music channels (a brand under apps/lyrics_videos/brands/, e.g. INVERTED Devils, Subhodayam) fro…
skills.description: Write the YouTube title and description for a song on one of the user's music channels (a brand under apps/lyrics_videos/brands/, e.g. INVERTED Devils, Subhodayam) from the song's title and its lyrics.json (or any lyrics file). The description is a 2-line intro to the song, the plain lyrics (no timestamps, no section labels), a 1-line outro about the channel and at most 5 hashtags, in the channel's voice; checked against YouTube's limits and saved as title.txt / description.txt. Use when the user says "YouTube title and description for <song>", "write the description with lyrics", "YouTube metadata", "/write-youtube-metadata", or as the metadata step of pack-youtube. Append new user feedback to the log at the bottom.
